claim_ceiling: Corpus identity and declared arithmetic contracts only. This fixture does not establish physical model accuracy, asteroid resource abundance, recoverable reserves, economic viability, hardware or flight qualification.

source_records.title: Optical Mining of Asteroids, Moons, and Planets to Enable Sustainable Human Exploration and Space Industrialization
source_records.caveat: NASA describes an 8 kW full-scale optical-mining demonstration using high-fidelity CI-type asteroid simulant in vacuum and sunlight from a 10 m diameter concentrator. Do not infer operational mission performance or unreported accepted-product throughput.

source_records.title: Optical mining of carbonaceous chondrite simulants: Testing and lessons learned in asteroid mining research
source_records.caveat: Vacuum optical-mining experiments report irradiance-, morphology- and failure-regime-dependent excavation and water production; organic vapour deposition can hamper operation. Reproduce only accessible source data and preserve the exact Nectar material identity.

source_records.title: Asteroid laser mining under cryogenic vacuum conditions: Particle ejection and Fe-Ni enrichment from asteroid simulants
source_records.caveat: C- and S-type simulants were irradiated for 30 s at 300, 600 and 900 W using a continuous-wave fibre laser in a chamber at 10^-2 Pa and 253 K. Fe-Ni-enriched ejected fines are not refined or qualified metal.

source_records.title: Thermal extraction of H2O(s) from lunar regolith simulant with concentrated solar irradiation: Experimental analysis
source_records.caveat: High-vacuum lunar simulant experiments provide adjacent receiver/process evidence, not asteroid results. The reported indirect-receiver sublimation improvement is source-specific and must not be generalized.

source_records.title: Prototype Demonstration of Solar-Carbothermal System to Extract Oxygen From Regolith
source_records.caveat: NASA reports an integrated concentrator/reactor/control prototype using simulated lunar regolith and confirms carbon monoxide production. Do not promote this to a deployed lunar plant or purified oxygen production.

source_records.title: Phased-array beaming of laser power from cislunar space to the lunar surface
source_records.caveat: End-to-end cislunar laser-beaming model with time-dependent visibility, divergence, jitter, conversion and thermal/dust limits. Numerical delivered-energy cases are model results, not flight demonstrations.

source_records.title: Design Study of Surface to Surface Laser Power Beaming on the Moon
source_records.caveat: The 300 W continuous, 10 km, five-year and under-625 kg figures are source-defined design requirements, not demonstrated lunar service.

source_records.title: Fission Surface Power
source_records.caveat: NASA/DOE are designing a 40 kWe-class lunar surface fission system for a future demonstration. It is a competing design reference, not a currently deployed lunar plant.

cases.note: Preserve the 8 kW optical mining demonstration and 10 m concentrator as the source-reported experiment boundary; unreported yield remains null.
Use source-accessible per-sample irradiance and response data. Preserve the observed non-monotonic excavation response and organic-vapour fouling; do not create missing points.
The 300/600/900 W results belong to the reported 30 s, 10^-2 Pa, 253 K chamber experiment. Ejected Fe-Ni-enriched fines are not refined metal.
Use the vacuum ice/regolith receiver experiments to inform lunar design comparisons only; do not transfer results to asteroid compositions.
Keep CO detection, inferred process progression and accepted purified oxygen as different evidence states.
Use the end-to-end chain and delivered daily energy; do not compare optical aperture power directly with receiver load energy.
The design specifies a 300 W continuous user load up to 10 km, five-year lifetime and under-625 kg landed mass; verify the source's entire energy chain and duty cycle.
Compare continuous firm power as a service alternative, with realistic landed mass, radiator, fuel, shielding and mission constraints when source data are available.
Inverse-square solar flux check; not an orbit, site illumination or collector performance prediction.
Finite solar angular diameter produces a broad focal image; optical aberrations and nonuniformity are not modeled.
The solar angular diameter decreases inversely with heliocentric distance; this is a geometric focal-image screen, not a collector or asteroid thermal-process model.
An ideal 10 m circular collector focused at 100 m at 1 AU produces a 0.93 m solar image and about 115.6x geometric concentration before optical losses.
Ideal circular-aperture Airy first-null diameter; excludes beam quality, jitter, pointing error, receiver capture and laser safety.
All input feedstock mass is assigned to residue, captured/escaped solids, captured/escaped gas and other declared mass.
Captured gas cannot be promoted to accepted product when independent assay purity is below the specified product contract.
An energy stage exceeds the immediately preceding meter plane and must be rejected.
A downstream measurement cannot be promoted when an upstream stage is unknown.
